requirement_text.REQ-134: config/test.exs sets token_verifier: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifierDouble, so the entire suite passes with no identity provider running. That was correct while none existed. Its consequence is that no test in this repository has ever exercised a real token, which is why a placeholder issuer and an unmountable authorization matrix both survived to 2026-08-22 without a single failure. Add an integration path that obtains a real token from the running Keycloak (direct-access grant against the seeded users) and drives it through AuthPipeline for real: signature verification against the live JWKS, issuer/realm resolution, claim mapping, JIT provisioning, and the authorization plug. Keep TokenVerifierDouble as the default for the unit suite. Do NOT make the whole suite depend on a running Keycloak -- that would trade a blind spot for a flaky, infrastructure-coupled suite, and this project already runs partitioned parallel test processes (scripts/test_parallel.sh) that a shared external service would serialize. The real-token path should be a tagged/excluded-by-default set that a human or CI can run deliberately, with a clear skip message naming what has to be running -- follow the pattern web/tests/e2e/onboarding/ already uses ("Ensure docker-compose services are running"). State in the result how a developer runs it, and confirm that mix test with Keycloak stopped still passes.

task.description: Design (no implementation code) an integration test path that obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak via direct-access grant against the seeded bpm-default realm users, and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline for real -- real JWKS/signature verification via Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc, real issuer/realm resolution, real claim mapping, and real JIT provisioning. Must stay excluded from the default mix test / scripts/test_parallel.sh run (tagged, opt-in only), must not touch config/test.exs's TokenVerifierDouble default, and must specify an exact skip message and an exact developer-facing include command.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Wrote lib/letflow/design/req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md. Design: test/test_helper.exs gains `exclude: [:keycloak]` on ExUnit.start/1 (applies to plain `mix test`, any path-scoped mix test, and every scripts/test_parallel.sh partition alike, since all load the same test_helper.exs) -- this is what keeps the new suite out of the default run without touching config/test.exs's TokenVerifierDouble default. New tagged module test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs (@moduletag :keycloak, async: false -- it temporarily overrides Application.get_env(:letflow, :oidc)'s :token_verifier to the real Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc for its own setup/on_exit-bounded duration, restoring the double afterward). setup_all probes Keycloak's realm discovery endpoint via a new test-support module test/support/keycloak_test_client.ex (Erlang :httpc/:inets, no new mix.exs dependency) with a short timeout and returns {:skip, <message>} on failure; exact skip text specified: 'Keycloak not ready at <discovery-url>. Ensure docker-compose services are running (docker compose up -d keycloak) before executing these tests.' KeycloakTestClient also specifies direct_access_token/4 (resource-owner-password grant against Keycloak's token endpoint, client_id letflow-web per priv/keycloak/realms/bpm-default.json) and tamper_signature/1 (mutates a real JWT's signature segment byte-for-bit) with full @specs and error shapes. Design specifies ensure_bpm_default_tenant!/0 (get-or-create, not a plain insert, since slug/idp_realm_id are uniquely constrained and this fixture is deliberately NOT torn down between runs) that provisions the pinned bpm-default tenant row (Letflow.Identity.Tenant's @default_tenant_slug pinning requires idp_realm_id == 'bpm-default' exactly) and its schema via the same TenantProvisioning steps test/support/tenant_fixture.ex already establishes. AC1: builds a conn via Plug.Test, calls AuthPipeline.call/2 with a genuine admin-user token, asserts refute conn.halted and conn.assigns.auth_context shape (tenant_id/user_id/roles, PLATFORM_ADMIN present). AC2: same pipeline call with KeycloakTestClient.tamper_signature/1 applied to a genuine token, with the real Oidcc verifier still active -- asserts conn.halted and conn.status == 401, explicitly reasoning that TokenVerifierDouble could not even express this case (it only recognizes one fixed sentinel string). AC3: designer-user token, Repo.aggregate count query against Letflow.Identity.User (external_realm/external_id, scoped via prefix: schema_name) before/after-first/after-second AuthPipeline calls -- 0 -> 1 -> 1, plus user_id equality across both calls as the row-identity proof. AC4: exact commands named -- `mix test` and `scripts/test_parallel.sh`, both unaffected by Keycloak's state because of the test_helper.exs exclusion; TEST-RUNNER's future evidence is that command's real output with the keycloak docker-compose service stopped. AC5: setup_all's ExUnit {:skip, message} mechanism (not a raised exception, which would report as a failure rather than a skip) with the exact message text quoted above. AC6: exact command `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs`, stated verbatim in the design's own S2 section for downstream steps to reuse without reinventing it. No implementation code included -- signatures, @specs, error-shape atoms, and exact string/command literals only. Every acceptance criterion is cross-referenced to a concrete design section in the doc's closing table (S10); no open questions were left unresolved (S9).

Rework 1/3 (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL on check 2e): sections 7.1-7.4 originally contained compilable ExUnit `setup do...end`/`test "..." do...end` blocks with real Plug.Test/AuthPipeline.call/Repo.aggregate/assert-refute code -- actual test implementation, not a design-level description. Rewrote all four subsections as numbered-step prose contracts (what is provisioned, what is called, what shape/value is asserted, in plain English matched to section 4.1's own signature-only register) with zero `assert`/`refute`/`test "..." do`/`setup do` tokens remaining anywhere in the file (verified by grep after the edit). No substantive content was dropped: the real-verifier override's on-entry/on-exit behavior (7.1), the genuine-token/AuthPipeline/auth_context-shape check (7.2, AC1), the tamper-then-401 check under the same real-verifier override (7.3, AC2), and the three-count-query plus user_id-equality two-call JIT check (7.4, AC3) are all still fully specified, just as prose contracts instead of code bodies. Section 4.1 (KeycloakTestClient), the test_helper.exs exclusion mechanism (S2), the skip message (S3), and the tenant fixture provisioner (S5) -- all of which the validator confirmed already passed -- were left unchanged.
